candidate.title: Adaptive laboratory evolution of E. coli W under glycerol limitation
candidate.intervention: serial batch cultivation in 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) medium, 250 mL flask, 37 degC with agitation, transfer every 12 h, initial OD600 stepwise 0.0008 -> 0.0004 -> 0.00016, ~1300 generations (Eq. 1)
candidate.replicates: unknown (Fig. 1 caption missing; number of parallel lineages not stated in available text)
candidate.readouts: estimated doubling time over generations (Fig. 1B), specific growth rate (Fig. 1C), glycerol consumption rate (Fig. 1D)
candidate.outcomes: single clone CY02 isolated; growth rate 0.67 +/- 0.03 -> 0.94 +/- 0.01 /hr (~40% increase); increased glycerol consumption rate; negligible fitness change on glucose
candidate.notes: Results text for this experiment is embedded in paragraph 1_introduction_p003 due to a parser section-misattribution; Fig. 1 caption absent.

candidate.title: Whole-genome resequencing and causal-mutation nomination
candidate.readouts: mutation calls vs NC_017635.1 after parental background subtraction
candidate.analysis: shared-mutation focus between population and CY02 (Table 1, Fig. S1)
candidate.outcomes: 93 (population) / 89 (CY02) total mutations; 30 / 28 new; shared notable: glpK T235M, crp R209H, ptsP Pro174fs, rsfS Gln6*, mglC Asn4fs

candidate.title: Reverse engineering of glpK^m/crp^m and fitness/GUR characterization
candidate.intervention: lambda-Red recombinase-mediated introduction of glpK T235M and crp R209H singly and in combination into parental W
candidate.conditions: M9 minimal glycerol medium; exponential growth
candidate.readouts: specific growth rate (Fig. 2A), specific glycerol uptake rate (Fig. 2B, Cedex)
candidate.outcomes: growth: glpK^m 1.45-fold (p<0.022), double 1.56-fold (p=0.037), CY02 1.63-fold (p=0.009), crp^m n.s.; GUR: 1.78/1.70/1.60-fold for glpK^m strains, crp^m n.s.

candidate.title: GlpK^w vs GlpK T235M expression, purification and enzyme kinetics
candidate.intervention: cloning of WT/mutant glpK into pET28a(+) (N-terminal 6xHis), overexpression in BL21(DE3), Ni-NTA purification
candidate.conditions: assay at 25 degC, pH 7.0, 200 uL reaction, 0.5 ug/mL enzyme; FBP 0-10 mM for allostery
candidate.replicates: six replicates (WT enzyme), five replicates (mutant enzyme) per Fig. 2D caption; replicate type unspecified
candidate.readouts: V0/Vmax, specific activity vs FBP; Vmax, Km_gly, kcat, kcat/Km, FBP K0.5 (Table 2)
candidate.analysis: SigmaPlot 12 curve fitting; Eq. (4) allosteric fit
candidate.outcomes: catalytic activity unchanged; mutant insensitive to FBP (K0.5 >10,000 uM vs 0.386 mM WT per text)

candidate.title: Intracellular cAMP measurement
candidate.conditions: exponential phase harvest; ice-cold 65% ethanol extraction
candidate.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
candidate.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains ~2% of WT; CY02 ~20% of WT; crp^m 36% of WT; all P<0.001

candidate.title: RT-qPCR of glpK expression
candidate.controls: wild-type; normalization to rrsA or ihfB
candidate.readouts: relative glpK mRNA abundance (Fig. S4, unavailable)
candidate.analysis: StepOne Software v2.3; standard-curve primer efficiency
candidate.outcomes: glpK^m-harboring strains 3-6% of WT; crp^m ~22%; double mutant < half of glpK^m

candidate.title: RNA-seq transcriptome comparison WT vs CY02
candidate.conditions: M9 minimal + 2 g/L glycerol; harvest OD600 0.4-0.5
candidate.readouts: gene expression; DEGs; CRP regulon enrichment
candidate.analysis: CLC Genomics Workbench trimming/mapping; DESeq2 (FC>2, adj P<0.01)
candidate.outcomes: 640 DEGs (149 up / 491 down); 181 CRP-regulated DEGs; 148/157 positively regulated CRP genes downregulated; lower glycolysis up, TCA/respiration down, pta/ackA up, acs down

candidate.title: Acetate secretion rate measurement
candidate.analysis: one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc
candidate.outcomes: WT below accurate determination; CY02 and glpK^m-harboring mutants elevated; crp^m not determinable

candidate.title: GABA production in M9 glycerol minimal medium
candidate.conditions: 50 mL M9 glycerol (0.2% v/v) + 50 mg/L yeast extract, 250 mL flasks, biological triplicates
candidate.outcomes: 0.06 +/- 0.01 g/L for both WT and CY02 (negligible difference)

candidate.title: Medium and glycerol-concentration optimization for GABA production
candidate.intervention: switch to amino acid-rich LB + glycerol; glycerol concentration screen using growth rate as proxy (Fig. S7, plate reader)
candidate.conditions: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol selected; stationary-phase GABA measurement
candidate.readouts: specific growth rate (proxy screen); final GABA concentration
candidate.outcomes: highest growth at 2% glycerol; stationary GABA: WT 0.05, crp^m 0.06, glpK^m 0.07, double 0.07, CY02 0.17 g/L
candidate.notes: Fig. S7 data unavailable; proxy assumption (growth-coupled GABA production) is an author assumption, not validated causality.

candidate.title: Time-course GABA production WT vs CY02 in LB + 2% glycerol
candidate.conditions: 50 mL LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, 250 mL flasks, 37 degC, 200 rpm, over 24 h, biological triplicates
candidate.readouts: growth, glycerol consumption (HPLC-RID), GABA (dansyl chloride HPLC-UV 286 nm)
candidate.outcomes: WT max 0.15 +/- 0.01 g/L, 0.03 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr; CY02 0.39 +/- 0.03 g/L, 0.08 +/- 0.01 g/L/hr (~2.6-fold); glycerol consumption similar

candidate.title: Targeted knockout of metabolic sinks (ackA, mgsA, gabT) in CY02 and WT backgrounds
candidate.intervention: lambda-Red KanR replacement and pCP20 marker excision to delete ackA, mgsA, gabT singly, in double combinations, and as triple knockout
candidate.conditions: LB + 2% (v/v) glycerol, flask batch, biological triplicates
candidate.readouts: growth, glycerol consumption, GABA titer/productivity (Fig. 6, Fig. S8, Table 3)
candidate.outcomes: single KOs lower than comparator; doubles 0.46/0.45/0.37 g/L; CY02_TKO 0.59 +/- 0.04 g/L and 0.13 +/- 0.02 g/L/hr (1.5-/1.6-fold over CY02; 3.9-/4.3-fold over WT); benefit of double/triple KOs absent in WT background; ΔackA strains prolonged lag phase
